# toInteger

<link-summary>Reads a number out of a value, or reports that there is none.</link-summary>

<web-summary>toInteger() — Reads a number out of a value, or reports that there is none. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function toInteger(value: unknown): number | null;
```

A string is read with `parseInt`, which takes the leading digits and stops: `"12abc"` gives `12`. Text with no leading digits, an empty string, `null` and `undefined` all give `null`, so the failure is a value you can check rather than a `NaN` that spreads.

A number passes through untouched — including a fractional one, which is why `toInteger(1.9)` is `1.9` and not `1`. Reach for `Math.trunc` or `requireInteger` when a whole number is what the call actually needs.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description        |
| :-------- | :-------- | :----------------- |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to read. |

## Returns

`number | null` — the number, or `null` when there is none to read.

## Examples

### Reading a number

```javascript
toInteger(" 42 "); // => 42
toInteger("12abc"); // => 12
toInteger("abc"); // => null
toInteger(null); // => null
toInteger(1.9); // => 1.9
```
